title: introduce-tenant-hook-operator-and-values-decomposition
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: the private-installer chart has accumulated a large, hard-to-navigate values.yaml and a set of ad-hoc init hooks that vary per-tenant. This PR extracts a small, tenant-scoped 'hook-operator' component and decomposes the monolithic values file into a modular schema so operators can opt into the operator-driven init flow or continue using the legacy init hooks. The change aims to make tenant init sequencing observable, easier to test in isolation, and more robust for multi-network deployments.

What I changed: 1) Added a new subchart charts/hook-operator that runs as a lightweight controller which sequences tenant-scoped init Jobs via Kubernetes native leader election and CRD-free config (uses ConfigMap-driven plans). 2) Decomposed charts/private-installer/values.yaml into charts/private-installer/values.schema.json and layered values under charts/private-installer/values/ (tenantDefaults.yaml, initPipelines.yaml, networkProfiles.yaml). 3) Replaced inline init hooks with templated helper functions in charts/_helpers.tpl and introduced a new annotation convention chart.redwood.ai/init-sequence to let the operator claim and run steps. 4) Added a new migration helper script scripts/migrate-values.py to assist large customers in moving to the new structure. 5) Updated README and examples under examples/private-installer/ to show both operator-enabled and legacy-hook install paths.

Risk and compatibility: default behavior is unchanged unless operator.enabled is explicitly turned on. The operator is opt-in to reduce blast radius for existing installs. Migration path documented and a helm test/upgrade checklist is included in the notes.

Testing and verification: unit tests for templating helpers added, chart lint passes (helm template + kubeval), integration smoke e2e run against KIND that exercises multi-tenant sequencing, and manual upgrade tests against a staging cluster using a representative multi-network config. CI: all checks passed on the final run.

Rollback plan: operator can be disabled and tenant-managed Jobs re-enabled by flipping values.operator.enabled=false and restoring legacy values from values/tenantDefaults.yaml backups. For critical failures the chart ships a rollback hook that attempts to surface job logs to a named ConfigMap to speed debugging.

Related: ENG-1243 (tenant init reliability), OPS-870 (on-prem installer ergonomics).

release_notes: Introduce an opt-in tenant-scoped hook-operator and split private-installer values into modular files. Default install path unchanged. Operators can opt-in to add more reliable init sequencing and better observability for tenant installs. Migration helper script included.
notes: Operator is expressly opt-in to avoid changing behavior for existing customers. See migration section in README-private-installer.md; recommend rolling upgrades with canary tenant before enabling operator across all tenants.
